Nero
nē´rō
n. (Nero Claudius Caesar, 37–68, Roman emperor from 54, the Caesar to whom Paul appealed and the first emperor to persecute Christians at Rome)
Latin Nero, a Sabine cognomen said to mean strong, valiant. Not named in the New Testament, which calls him simply Caesar.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Nero was emperor when Paul wrote to the Romans, and that fact gives Romans 13 its edge: “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God” (Rom 13:1) was written to Christians living under the man who would burn them. It was to Nero's court that Paul appealed from Festus: “I appeal unto Caesar” (Act 25:11). During his Roman imprisonment the gospel reached the palace itself, for he sends greetings from “they that are of Caesar's household” (Php 4:22). After the great fire of Rome in 64, Nero fastened the blame on the Christians, and the historian Tacitus records that they were torn by dogs, crucified, and burned as torches in his gardens. The church has always held that Peter and Paul died at Rome in his reign. Paul's last letter shows the spirit in which he faced it: “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me” (2Ti 4:16); “Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me” (2Ti 4:17). Nero died by his own hand in 68, abandoned by the senate and the guard.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines tyrant as a despot; a monarch or other ruler who uses power to oppress his subjects; a person who exercises unlawful authority, or lawful authority in an unlawful manner.

expand to see more

TYRANT, n. A monarch or other ruler or master, who uses power to oppress his subjects.

2. A despotic ruler; a cruel master; an oppressor.

3. Among the ancient Greeks, one who seized the government of a state without right.

Key Scripture

Rom 13:1 — "Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God."

Act 25:11 — "For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar."

Php 4:22 — "All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household."

2Ti 4:17 — "Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion."

Modern Corruption

Nero is the test case for Romans 13, and both its modern misreadings — that Christians owe any government unlimited obedience, and that a wicked government forfeits all obedience — break against him.

expand to see more

One misreading treats Romans 13 as a charter for whatever the state commands; but Paul, who wrote it, disobeyed Rome's ban on preaching Christ and died for it. The opposite misreading treats any unjust ruler as no ruler at all; but Paul wrote of Nero's government as ordained of God and appealed to its courts. Paul held both: the office is God's, and the ruler answers to God for how he bears it.

The recovery is the apostolic pattern: honour the office, use the courts, pray for rulers, obey in all things lawful, refuse what God forbids, and suffer what must be suffered. The Christians in Nero's gardens did not revolt, and they did not deny Christ. Their blood, not their politics, conquered Rome.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek exousia (G1849), power, authority; epikaleo (G1941), to appeal to, call upon; endunamoo (G1743), to strengthen.

expand to see more

Greek exousia (G1849) — authority, power; Romans 13:1–2.

Greek epikaleo (G1941) — to call upon, appeal to; Acts 25:11, 12.

Greek endunamoo (G1743) — to empower, strengthen; 2 Timothy 4:17, Philippians 4:13.

Usage

"“there is no power but of God” (Rom 13:1) — written to Christians under Nero."

"“I appeal unto Caesar” (Act 25:11) — Paul's use of Nero's courts."

"“chiefly they that are of Caesar's household” (Php 4:22) — the gospel inside Nero's palace."
